library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Pinning commons-io alone probably isn't enough. Gradle still has to evaluate the `[2.4,]` range from the library's POM edge. In the test build.gradle, declare the library dependency with `exclude group: 'commons-io', module: 'commons-io'`, and keep the explicit commons-io:2.11.0 testImplementation dependency. Do this only where the tested version is 4.14 or another version whose POM carries the same range, for example by checking `libraryVersion`. Versions up to 4.13.1 already resolve. The 4.14 POM also declares open-ended ranges on optional dependencies, such as `bcprov-jdk15on:[1.52,]` (optional). If a later resolution error names one of those, exclude it or pin a concrete version in the same way. No Docker image, system property or environment variable is needed.
risks: If a direct dependency without an exclusion does not stop Gradle from evaluating the range, resolution will keep failing until the exclusion is applied.
Other open-ended ranges in the 4.14 POM, such as the bouncycastle ones, may surface as the next resolution failure.
The existing tests may need to stay compatible with 4.0 through 4.14. Keep the version-conditional dependency logic minimal.
